workflow.title: Logical work order
workflow.body: You can create samples from **Preselection** or from the **main page**. In Preselection you queue interesting requests for OGM; when you create the Bionano number they go into the database with the same request and diagnosis. On the main page you can add and edit samples directly.

status.title: Sample status
status.body: The icon to the left of the BN no. shows status. In edit mode you can change it; if you cancel without saving, it reverts.

actions.title: Actions
actions.hacer: **Prepare**: process samples you have entered that are not yet extracted.
actions.leerExtraido: **Read extracted**: once extracted, used to enter extracted concentrations.
actions.tirar: **Discard**: for those with little extracted material.
actions.pteChip: **Pending chip**: for labeled and quantified samples pending loading.

other.title: Other screens
other.chips: **Chips**: manage chips and FC slots linked to labeled readings.
other.calidad: **Quality**: lot catalog (extraction, labeling, membrane and chip) and air-filter change log.
other.lotes: **Lots**: catalog of extraction, labeling, membrane and chip lots, with the linked samples, readings and chips.
other.calcs: **Calculations**: lab utilities (e.g. dilutions) from already recorded data.
other.options: **Options**: profile, variables, tags, statistics, documents, export, appearance and manual.

roles.title: Roles and users
roles.body: The user role is for viewing samples. The admin role can add samples and manage catalogs and tags. New users are created with the **master code** set when configuring the app.

edit.title: Edit and save
edit.body: On the main page, **Edit** lets you change data and status. **Save** confirms changes; **Cancel** discards everything unsaved, including the status color.

author.title: Author
author.body: BionApp was conceived, designed and developed by <github>GenDoc94</github> (Juan José Domínguez-García, <orcid>ORCID</orcid>).

origin.title: Project origin
origin.body: It is an original idea by GenDoc94, continued from a previous project also called **BionApp**, created and developed 100% by the author in Microsoft Access. This version (online and desktop) is the improved evolution of that app: the same OGM sample workflow, with a modern UI, multi-user support, and web or local use.

version.title: Current version
version.intro: BionApp v{{version}} (beta). There are two editions with the same business logic:
version.online: **Online**: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router, Supabase (Auth, Postgres, Edge Functions, storage) and web hosting (e.g. Vercel).
version.desktop: **Desktop**: Electron, React, Vite (electron-vite), Tailwind CSS, SQLite (better-sqlite3), local authentication (bcrypt) and data in a user-chosen folder.
version.common: Shared UI: Radix UI components, Lucide icons and Sonner notifications. MIT license (link in the app footer).

ai.title: Use of artificial intelligence
ai.body1: Artificial intelligence was used to generate application code. The original software idea, foundations, full app architecture and intended use are by GenDoc94. AI is an implementation tool; it is not the author of the product or its laboratory design.
ai.disclaimer: BionApp was not created by a professional software engineer, but by a physician interested in computing. There may be code errors and even conceptual ones. The author is not liable for damage, data loss, clinical or laboratory decisions, or any other harm arising from use of this application. It is provided as-is, in beta, under the MIT license.

cite.title: How to cite
cite.body: If you use BionApp in a paper, cite it with the data in <citation>CITATION.cff</citation> (author, ORCID and DOI <doi>{{doi}}</doi>).

thanks.title: Acknowledgements
thanks.body: Thanks to the open-source communities and projects that make this stack possible, and to those who use BionApp in day-to-day lab work.

docs.title: Protocols and documents
docs.help: Files are stored in the `documentos/` folder inside this install’s shared data folder.
docs.empty: No documents. Upload PDF, Word or other protocol files for the technique.

export.title: Export database
export.help: Export all tables from the data folder. Excel and JSON produce a ZIP with one file per table. SQLite copies the local database to a `.sqlite` file. A dialog will open to choose the location.
